Or if expecting minutes, then "2"? We'll guess "120" because typical wait times might be in ms or secs. Wait time could be in ms but 2 min would be 120000ms. Hmm ambiguous. I'll choose "120" meaning 120 seconds.

So argv will be a string representation of a Java array of Strings. That means we need to produce something like "[\"-waitTime\", \"120\", \"-debuggeeName\", \"TestDebuggee\"]"

Also out needs to be a string representation of a Java PrintStream. So we can say "PrintStream(testLogStream)" or simply "testLogStream". They said "output the logs to a specific print stream testLogStream." So I think we can put "testLogStream" as the value.


> argv: string,

It seems each property is typed as string, but the content may be a string representation of a Java array. However, the example earlier shows passing an array directly. I'm going to follow the pattern used previously: Provide the array itself. Because the system likely interprets this correctly.
